'''Johannes Falnes''' (1931–2024) was a [[Professor Emeritus]] of [[Experimental Physics]] at the Department of Physics of the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] noted for his contributions to [[wave energy]] research. He was one of the pioneers of modern wave energy research.

==Education==
Falnes received his master's and doctoral degrees both from the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Peaks and troughs of wave energy: the dreams and the reality – speaker biographies |url=http://royalsociety.org/events/wave-energy-biographies/ |access-date=24 October 2011 |publisher=royalsociety.org}}</ref>

==Career==
Falnes spent his career at the Norwegian Institute of Technology (1956–1959), [[CERN]] (1959–1961), the [[University of Bergen]] (1961–1964), the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]]/[[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (1965–2001), and [[SINTEF]] (1966–1972), before retiring in 2002. 

Falnes' main research interest has been ocean wave energy and its utilisation. Together with [[Kjell Budal]], he initiated wave energy research in Norway in the 1970s. Falnes and Budal discovered the so-called antenna effect, where a floating point absorber could theoretically absorb far more wave energy from the sea than that which is directly incident upon its geometry, analogous to a radio antenna's ability to absorb radio waves.<ref>{{cite web |title=The economics and technology of taming Atlantic waves |url=http://www.waveenergy.ie/ |access-date=22 December 2009 |publisher=waveenergy.ie}}</ref> They also developed the latching control strategy to maximize energy extraction.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Drew |first1=B. |last2=Plummer |first2=A. R. |last3=Sahinkaya |first3=M. N. |year=2009 |title=A review of wave energy converter technology |journal=[[Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part A: Journal of Power and Energy]] |volume=223 |issue=8 |pages=887–902 |bibcode=2009PIMEA.223..887D |doi=10.1243/09576509JPE782 |s2cid=17186882}}</ref>

In December 2006, a seminar titled Challenges for Wave Energy Technology was dedicated in tribute to Falnes on his 75th anniversary. The seminar was held in [[Trondheim]], Norway. Wave energy experts such as [[Stephen Salter]] ([[University of Edinburgh]]), António Falcão ([[Instituto Superior Técnico]]), Alain Clément ([[École centrale de Nantes]]), and [[Richard Yemm]] ([[Ocean Power Delivery]]) addressed various topics in the seminar.<ref>{{cite web |title=Challenges for Wave Energy Technology |url=http://www.cesos.ntnu.no/activities/seminars/Falnes_Seminar/index.php |access-date=22 December 2009 |publisher=cesos.ntnu.no}}</ref>

Falnes is a member of The [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Akademimedlemmer, Fysikk |url=http://www.dknvs.no/akademimedlemmer/medlemmer/gruppe-ii-fysikk/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009020402/http://www.dknvs.no/akademimedlemmer/medlemmer/gruppe-ii-fysikk/ |archive-date=9 October 2016 |access-date=20 July 2016 |publisher=[[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]] |language=Norwegian}}</ref> and the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Medlemmer: FALNES, Johannes |url=http://www.ntva.no/index.php?option=com_club&view=member&id=120%3Afalnes-johannes&Itemid=60 |access-date=4 December 2012 |publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]] |language=Norwegian}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Among his pastimes are hiking and [[cross-country skiing]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Johannes Falnes |url=https://folk.ntnu.no/falnes/index-e.html |access-date=18 June 2024}}</ref>
